question: With the twist set explicitly, is the 3 x 1 weave pair gapped in both sectors to width 21; does its pair-count distance step outward without skipping (single-row or two-row tick); are the two arrangements one up to a symmetry of the weave?

definitions.antiperiodic sector: every knot crossing the seam reads column 0 flipped
definitions.two-row tick: the even-r and odd-r subsequences of |C(r)| each strictly decrease (declared as an envelope reading)
definitions.splitting: the difference of the top flip-even log eigenvalues per row between the sectors

forbidden_inputs: Changing arrangements, widths, sectors, readings, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
cheapest_meaningful_control: Plain NAE (critical, known numbers); the seam moved one column.

predictions.Q1: a point symmetry carries arr1's inconsistent bonds onto arr2's
predictions.Q2: same spectra at w/3 even; arr1 anti = arr2 per at w/3 odd (1e-6)
predictions.Q5: single-row ruler fails at 0, 2; two-row tick holds everywhere
predictions.Q6: tau slope on r = 10-30 within 10% of the width-12 spin gap

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as stated in the pre-registration

stop_rule: One run; A97 status; referee hand-off; report.
